set.approach: Start at the Payne Creek and Brookside trailhead west of Bailey and follow the Brookside trail up steep switchbacks to the crest of the Platte River Mountains. Leave the trail there and head east through fairly open forest toward the boulderfield on the side of Payne Benchmark, then drop through it to Snowpack Ridge. This tower is the second one up, directly above the small tower at the base of the ridge.
set.descent_text: From the top of the tower, downclimb moderate ground higher up the ridge.

review.notes: Approach from area Getting There plus route Location; descent from route text. Single source, no numbers.

set.approach: Start at the Payne Creek and Brookside trailhead west of Bailey and follow the Brookside trail up steep switchbacks to the crest of the Platte River Mountains. Leave the trail there and head east through fairly open forest toward the boulderfield on the side of Payne Benchmark, then drop through it to Snowpack Ridge. The crack is on the west face at the very top of the ridge, above the steep part of the face and before the wall becomes much smaller.

review.notes: Approach from area page; location from route page. Route tops out on the ridge but no source gives a descent, so none written.

set.approach: Start at the Payne Creek and Brookside trailhead west of Bailey and follow the Brookside trail up steep switchbacks to the crest of the Platte River Mountains. Leave the trail there and head east through fairly open forest toward the boulderfield on the side of Payne Benchmark, then drop through it to Snowpack Ridge. It is the lowest and smallest of the towers, where the ridge begins, and the line goes up its west side.
set.descent_text: Downclimb the easy ground on the east face of the tower.

review.notes: Approach from area page; descent and location from route page.

set.approach: Leave the car at the overlook near mile 16 of the Pikes Peak Highway, cross the low wall and walk down the drainage keeping the formation to your right. Work low, then climb back up to the foot of the route, using the slabby rib that guards the base of the formation. The route is on the north-northeast face, on the right side, and is recognisable by the roof on its first pitch.
set.descent_text: Top out the formation, then walk south along the summit crest toward the road, keeping to the west side until grassy ledges let you step down into the drainage again. Some routes on the formation have a non-permanent rappel line.

review.notes: Area page Getting There and Descent, written for all routes topping out on the formation; route page for face and start.

set.approach: The towers sit on the south side of the interstate in the canyon between Frisco and Copper Mountain. Reach them by taking the bike path from Copper toward Frisco, leaving the bikes after a few miles and hiking the gully directly below the towers. At the top of the avalanche chute, follow the ledge system left to the base of Tower 1. The route is on the left side of the west-facing cliff and goes through steep ground to a recognisable offwidth.
set.descent_text: Walk south along the crest to the anchors of the neighbouring line, The White Spirit, and rappel it. Alternatively, drop through a small notch near the top of the route onto the back of the tower and hike off around it, which involves about 60 feet of 5.2 downclimbing.

review.notes: Approach from the two area pages; descent and face from route page.

set.approach: The towers sit on the south side of the interstate in the canyon between Frisco and Copper Mountain. Reach them by taking the bike path from Copper toward Frisco, leaving the bikes after a few miles and hiking the gully directly below the towers. At the top of the avalanche chute, follow the ledge system left to the base of Tower 1. The route starts in a hand crack just left of The White Spirit, on the right side of the tower.
set.descent_text: Walk south along the crest to the bolted anchor atop The White Spirit and rappel that line all the way down.

review.notes: Approach from the two area pages; descent and start from route page. Rappel count left out (one source).

set.approach: The towers sit on the south side of the interstate in the canyon between Frisco and Copper Mountain. Reach them by taking the bike path from Copper toward Frisco, leaving the bikes after a few miles and hiking the gully directly below the towers. At the top of the avalanche chute, follow the ledge system left to the base of Tower 1. set.descent_text: Rappel the route on its bolted anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the area pages; route page says rappel the route. Count left out (one source).

set.approach: The towers sit on the south side of the interstate in the canyon between Frisco and Copper Mountain. Reach them by taking the bike path from Copper toward Frisco, leaving the bikes after a few miles and hiking the gully directly below the towers. Tower 2 is just uphill from Tower 1. Follow the avalanche chute as it branches left below a big slab, and after some fifth-class scrambling reach a two-bolt anchor in the chute, which marks the start.
set.descent_text: From the summit, rappel down the slab to the climber's left of the arete to the big ledge system, then rappel the lower two pitches of the climb to the ground.

review.notes: Approach from area pages and route Location; descent from route page. Rappel counts inconsistent in the source, so left out.

set.approach: The towers sit on the south side of the interstate in the canyon between Frisco and Copper Mountain. Reach them by taking the bike path from Copper toward Frisco, leaving the bikes after a few miles and hiking the gully directly below the towers. Tower 2 is just uphill from Tower 1. Continue up the gully that rises above where Giants vs. Dragons begins.
set.descent_text: Come down the gully on the right-hand side as you face the rock.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page plus area pages.

set.approach: Eldar Tower stands north of the upper alpine lake, reached by hiking west past Freya Tower from the Rock Creek trailhead on the east side of the Gore Range. Walk to the southeast corner of the peak, where a clean first pitch marks the start; easier, grungier variations exist on the south side.
set.descent_text: From the summit, follow fourth-class ground and a ledge system down eastward, curving round to the mountain's north side. Then locate the chute that faces south on the mountain's western flank and take it to the talus fan beneath.

review.notes: Approach: Eldar area page, Freya area page for the trailhead, route Location. Descent from route page.

set.approach: Eldar Tower stands north of the upper alpine lake, reached by hiking west past Freya Tower from the Rock Creek trailhead on the east side of the Gore Range. The route ascends the east face and shares its start with I Found The Letters, at the southeast corner of the peak.
set.descent_text: Walk off by curving around the tower's north aspect and dropping into the west-side chute.

review.notes: Approach as above; descent from route page.

set.approach: The spire is in the South Rock Creek drainage, a quarter mile south of Freya Tower. Begin at the Rock Creek trailhead on the east side of the Gore Range, take the Gore Range trail south for roughly a mile, then turn southwest into the woods and follow the broad ridge to treeline. Cross the boulderfield east and descend into Asgard Meadows beneath the north sides of the Freya and Thor towers, then continue south to the spire. The route starts on a low-angle ramp on the northeast side.
set.descent_text: Descend to the saddle on the back side of the spire, then follow the second south-facing chute to the west back to the base of the climb.

review.notes: Spire page defers to the Freya approach plus a quarter mile; Freya page gives trailhead and line.

set.approach: The spire is in the South Rock Creek drainage, a quarter mile south of Freya Tower. Begin at the Rock Creek trailhead on the east side of the Gore Range, take the Gore Range trail south for roughly a mile, then turn southwest into the woods and follow the broad ridge to treeline. Cross the boulderfield east and descend into Asgard Meadows beneath the north sides of the Freya and Thor towers, then continue south to the spire. The route starts at the beginning of the southern arete, in a hand and fist crack.
set.descent_text: After the short scramble to the summit, go down via the saddle on the back side of the spire and descend the second south-facing chute to the west.

review.notes: As above; descent from route page.

set.approach: Park where the other Halidome walls are reached from, then follow a tongue of talus up to the base of the West Tower's own approach gully. Pass two chockstones on short fixed lines, continue up loose talus and scree to the last chockstone, and climb the low fifth-class slab to its left on a fixed line. Keep going up the gully, hugging the right wall, to the base of the route.
set.descent_text: Either walk off or rappel the route on single-rope rappels to the top of the first pitch, after which a walk-off leads rightward. For the walk-off, climb up to the buttress crest above the final anchors, head west and descend the loose scree gully toward the road; a line of fourth-class and low fifth-class downclimbing in the same direction avoids the gully.

review.notes: Both from the area and route pages. Rappel count and times left out (one source).
